title: Application Inventory
description: Canonical semantic representation of the application produced by the Inventory Aggregator Agent. Transforms thousands of low-level DOM discoveries into a structured, business-oriented knowledge graph of the application — its modules, features, pages, workflows, entities, navigation, authentication, authorization, shared components, validation rules, business capabilities, integration points, and risk indicators. This is the primary knowledge source consumed by the Test Design Agent for test generation.

runId.description: Globally unique identifier for the test execution run. Must match the runId from test-run-request.json, crawl-package.json, and dom-inventory.json.

requestId.description: Correlation identifier from the originating HTTP request. Must match the requestId across all pipeline contracts.

applicationMetadata.description: Top-level metadata describing the application being analysed — its identity, version, technology stack, deployment target, and business context.

modules.description: Logical business modules discovered within the application. Each module represents a cohesive business domain such as Authentication, Administration, Sales, HR, or Inventory. Modules group related pages, features, entities, and workflows.

features.description: User-facing capabilities discovered in the application. Each feature represents a discrete unit of functionality from the user's perspective — Login, Search, Create User, Checkout, Export Report, Approve Request. Features reference the pages, forms, tables, and dialogs that implement them.

pages.description: Business-level page model enriched by the aggregator. Each page record references the lower-level pageId from dom-inventory.json and adds business context — module association, purpose, entry points, associated workflows, actions, and navigation targets. This is NOT a DOM page model.

workflows.description: End-to-end user workflows discovered or inferred from the application. Each workflow represents a complete user journey — Login Flow, Registration Flow, Checkout Flow, Approval Flow — with its trigger, steps, decision points, and exit states.

entities.description: Business entities discovered in the application. Each entity represents a core business concept — User, Customer, Invoice, Order, Product — with its attributes, associated data forms and tables, CRUD operations, and relationships to other entities.

navigationModel.description: High-level navigation model of the application. Describes how users traverse the application — entry points, global and module navigation structures, deep links, and cross-module navigation pathways.

authentication.description: Authentication mechanisms discovered in the application. Captures login methods, logout behaviour, session handling, password reset, MFA, and registration flows.

authorization.description: Authorization model of the application. Captures discovered roles, permission structures, protected pages and actions, and role dependency hierarchies.

sharedComponents.description: Reusable UI components and patterns discovered across the application. Each shared component represents a UI pattern that appears on multiple pages — Header, Footer, Sidebar, Search, Date Picker, Pagination, File Upload, Toast Notification, Modal Dialog.

validationRules.description: Aggregated validation rules discovered across all forms and inputs in the application. Each rule captures a distinct validation constraint — required fields, regex patterns, length limits, numeric ranges, business rules, and cross-field validations.

businessCapabilities.description: High-level business capabilities the application delivers. Each capability represents a significant area of business functionality — User Management, Reporting, Billing, Inventory Management, Workflow Automation, Document Management.

integrationPoints.description: External integration points discovered during analysis. Captures REST APIs, GraphQL endpoints, external login providers, payment gateways, maps, analytics services, storage providers, and email services.

riskIndicators.description: Areas of the application identified as high-risk for test design. Risk indicators flag regions that are likely to require deeper testing — large forms, complex tables, dynamic components, infinite scroll, nested dialogs, heavy JavaScript, file upload, authentication, authorization boundaries.

coverageSummary.description: Aggregated coverage and confidence metrics for the application inventory. Provides at-a-glance indicators for inventory completeness — total modules, features, workflows, entities, shared components, validation rules, and overall confidence.

inventoryMetadata.description: Metadata about the aggregation process itself — when it ran, which source contracts were consumed, the aggregator version, overall confidence, and any warnings or errors encountered.

uuid.description: A universally unique identifier in standard 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal format.

languages.description: All languages detected across the application. Populated when pages use multiple languages for internationalisation.

deploymentType.description: The deployment and rendering architecture of the application. Inferred from render mode analysis and framework detection.

pageCount.description: Total number of unique pages discovered and analysed across the application.
